message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it might be a STEMI, right?
reply:
**I don’t see a definite STEMI pattern on this image, but this ECG cannot rule out an acute heart attack.**

My tentative read is sinus rhythm around 75 beats/minute, with narrow QRS complexes and prominent upright T waves in the chest leads. The upward-sloping ST/T waves could look like ST elevation, but I don’t see convincing diagnostic elevation at the **J point**, where the QRS ends. There is some baseline noise.

An early coronary blockage can occur without classic STEMI criteria; symptoms, comparison with an old ECG, repeat ECGs, and troponin testing matter. [ACC guidance](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2022.08.750)

**If there is current or recent chest discomfort, breathlessness, sweating, or faintness, seek emergency assessment now; don’t drive yourself.** What symptoms prompted this ECG, and when did they start?
